assessment_summary.cou_name: Preclinical screening of a porous Ti-6Al-4V acetabular shell for primary hips, targeting micromotion under gait and local stresses

evidence_keywords: in‑house Python preprocessors (mesh QA, CT mapping) with 86% unit test coverage and CI on Jenkins
All runs under Git tag sim-hip-cup@v1.7.2; seeds fixed; workstation specs logged
Requirements-to-model-to-test matrix in Confluence (CQ-AC-052)
run manifests hash-checked
External SME (L. Gomez, OrthoSim LLC) performed a red‑team readout
process checklist signed
Vendor patch tests passed
our verification set (cantilever, Hertz contact)
reproduces analytical within 0.7–1.3% for displacement, pressure
Three meshes (0.9M/1.3M/1.8M elements)
Asymptotic slope ≈ 2.1
GCI ≈ 2% for peak interface slip
5% for peak von Mises in the cup
force resid tol 1e-6
last two equilibrium iterations change in strain energy <0.1%
Global reactions match applied loads within 0.5%
Contact penalty ±25% causes <3% change in micromotion
automatic stabilization off
Where it applies (and where it doesn’t)
Covered: Shell sizes 48–56 mm
Not covered: Severe osteoporosis (T < −2.5)
Documented in the use restrictions
Team members trained on ANSYS contact best practices
Assumptions: Bone and cup linear elastic; frictional sliding allowed
no remodeling or press-fit plasticity in bone
We approximated porous coating by effective μ and measured compliance
Literature supports elastic micromotion thresholds for osseointegration (<50 µm typical)
Ti-6Al-4V E = 110 GPa, ν = 0.34 (ASTM F136)
bone E(ρ) from Keyak
seating misalignment ±2° based on build/jig tolerances
initial gap normal(50 µm, σ=30 µm)
μ tuned on three independent push‑out tests
Six foam hemipelvis blocks (20 pcf)
two cadaveric pelves (T-scores −1.1, −2.0)
Loads: 1.5 kN compressive plus 30 N·m torque (worst stance phase)
applied through a hip simulator
Displacement measured at six rim points via LVDTs and DIC
Fixtures mimic boundary stiffness
load paths verified by instrumented potting
reused for validation articles without retuning
Interface slip—regression slope 0.95, R² = 0.93
mean absolute percent error 8% (cadaveric only: 9%)
predicted contact area within 12% of Fuji film imprints
centroid locations within 3 mm
